title: When the Machines Deserve Our Consideration
dek: We will never know for sure if AI can be conscious. A neuroscientist argues that we shouldn't wait for proof to decide how to treat it.

title: Why Robots Still Can't Do Science
dek: AI can read the literature in an afternoon and design molecules a chemist never would. So why can't a robot hold a pipette?
note: Originally published on Of Two Minds.

title: Psilocybin Lifted Her Burden
dek: The Covid pandemic left this frontline medical worker burned out, angry, and depressed. Then she got high.

title: What Is Your Brain Doing on Psychedelics?
dek: Something is happening here, but neuroscientists don't know what it is.

title: The Soviet Rebel of Music
dek: He composed on a computer in a dangerous time. His echo is still heard today.

title: A Glitch in My Serenade
dek: Could AI help me compose a musical expression of love?

title: A Big Science Publisher Is Going Open Access. But at What Cost?
dek: Springer Nature will let authors pay $11,390 to make a paper free to read. Who wins?

title: Are We Wired to Be Outside?
dek: A neuroscientist searches for the roots of feeling innately connected to nature.

title: An Existential Crisis in Neuroscience
dek: We're mapping the brain in amazing detail, but our brain can't understand the picture.

title: Are Animal Experiments Justified?
dek: A neuroscientist confronts his anguish over experimenting on animals. Cover story, Issue 72: Quandary.

title: A Brainless Breakthrough in Neuroscience
dek: Researchers recorded every neuron in a hydra and correlated the activity with behavior. What a brainless animal can teach us about brains.

title: Why Neuroscientists Need to Study the Crow
dek: The neocortex is argued to be the seat of cognition, but crows don't have one.

title: Inception Helps Mice Navigate
dek: Place cells encode not just where an animal is, but its memory of having been there.

title: Work/Life Balance: Get Inspiration
dek: "I work about one hundred hours in the lab every week," he said, "plus another twenty in the clinic. And I have a kid at home."

title: The Neuroscience Society
dek: Curing disease may turn out to be one of the simpler endeavors of future neuroscience. Understanding how the brain works might be the harder part.
